task_instance: Open a GitHub pull request (e.g. owner/repo#123) in the pr-artifact-explorer canvas and produce a shareable link/route for it, the skill's core open-and-share deliverable.
blocker_detail: The skill is entirely a driver for a host-provided 'Artifact Explorer' canvas: every action it describes (list_canvas_capabilities, open_canvas, invoke_canvas_action with open_target/share/open_runs/inspect_artifact/navigate_browser/screenshot/etc.) is a canvas tool that must be supplied by the host application. None of those canvas tools exist in this runtime's tool set, and the skill ships no bundled implementation (only SKILL.md is present beside it), so there is nothing to invoke. The deliverable also inherently needs reaching the GitHub hosting service over the network (disallowed in this air-gapped runtime) and a Chromium/Playwright browser for previews/screenshots (python 'playwright' module is absent and no chromium binary is installed). Per the run rules I must not write my own replacement/stub of the missing canvas or fabricate its responses.
evidence: Read SKILL.md: it states the action names are 'canvas actions, not standalone tools' and require list_canvas_capabilities/open_canvas/invoke_canvas_action on canvasId pr-artifact-explorer. `find .` over the skill repo returned only skills/pr-artifact-explorer/SKILL.md (no scripts/bundled canvas). My tool list contains no canvas-capability/open-canvas/invoke-canvas-action tools. Probes in the work dir: `python3 -c 'import playwright'` -> ModuleNotFoundError (no browser automation); no chromium/chromium-browser/google-chrome on PATH. The canvas runtime, GitHub network access, and a browser engine are all required and all absent, so no real deliverable could be opened, inspected, or shared and verified.
